entry.title: Applying Gemini 4 for large-scale codebase maintenance in Chromium

media:group.media:title: Applying Gemini 4 for large-scale codebase maintenance in Chromium
media:group.media:description:
The Chromium codebase is millions of lines long and decades old. In the past, working with it has meant navigating decades of tangled features, where touching one component can unexpectedly affect another. Erik Chen, an engineer at Google, is using Gemini 4 Argon to ‘untangle’ the architecture. The model’s coding capabilities mean that multiple agents can work independently to refactor the codebase (all verified by Chromium's test suites and code reviews from engineers). With Gemini 4 Argon maintaining the codebase, Erik and his team can focus their attention on the future of Chromium.
Learn more about Gemini 4 Argon: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-argon/

entry.title: Using Gemini 4 Argon to protect against Cyber attackers

media:group.media:title: Using Gemini 4 Argon to protect against Cyber attackers
media:group.media:description:
In shadow A/B testing on real-world systems, Wiz security researchers put Gemini 4 Argon to the test against complex cyber threats. Using its advanced reasoning and long-horizon capabilities, Gemini 4 Argon found over two times more vulnerabilities than baseline models and successfully uncovered critical risks—such as identifying a file download bypass and master key in healthcare software. By handling tireless, multi-step threat analysis and remediation, Gemini 4 gives defenders the crucial advantage needed to outpace attackers and protect sensitive data faster than ever before.
Learn more about Gemini 4 Argon: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-argon/

entry.title: Teaching a humanoid robot to play cornhole with Gemini 4 Argon

media:group.media:title: Teaching a humanoid robot to play cornhole with Gemini 4 Argon
media:group.media:description:
In an internal test, Google DeepMind robotics researchers instructed Gemini 4 Argon to watch a video of a human playing cornhole. Using its video understanding and advanced reasoning capabilities, Gemini 4 built a virtual simulation in MuJoCo and accurately calculated the physics and whole-body control required for Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid to sink seven consecutive shots in the real world. This Video-to-Sim-to-Real pipeline compresses weeks of manual modeling into a few hours, transforming ordinary videos into an infinite training ground for physical AI.
Learn more about Gemini 4 Argon: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-argon/

media:group.media:title: Untangling 500-page chemistry patents with Gemini 4
media:group.media:description:
Auditing chemistry literature usually means weeks of manual, error-prone reading, where a molecule’s structure can sit 50 pages away from its experimental readout. At Isomorphic Labs, researchers Brian Bender and Santosh Adhikari are using Gemini 4 Argon’s multimodal capabilities to help tackle this early research bottleneck. The model synthesizes dense papers and extracts patent data into structured reports in an afternoon instead of a month, helping teams uncover connected insights faster.

media:group.media:description:

From providing critical early warnings for Category 5 storms like Hurricane Melissa to predicting renewable energy supply and agricultural impacts, learn how models like WeatherNext 3 are building upon decades of numerical physics to reshape our understanding of the atmosphere.

entry.title: AlphaGenome Atlas: Understanding the human genome

media:group.media:title: AlphaGenome Atlas: Understanding the human genome
media:group.media:description:
We’ve used AlphaGenome to predict the molecular impact of every possible single-letter change in the human genome. All nine billion of them.
AlphaGenome Atlas is a 1PB dataset containing every single possible nucleotide variant alongside an AlphaGenome Variant Impact (AVI) score. This score helps researchers instantly understand the potential impact of any given variation.
AlphaGenome Atlas is available to researchers around the world, with coding and non-coding variations available.
Learn more: https://deepmind.google/blog/alphagenome-atlas-a-predictive-map-of-every-possible-dna-letter-change-in-the-human-genome
Disclaimer: The information provided by AlphaGenome Atlas is not intended to be a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment, and does not constitute medical or other professional advice. AlphaGenome has not been validated for, and is not approved for, any clinical use.

entry.title: WeatherNext 3: More accurate, timely, and local weather forecasts

media:group.media:title: WeatherNext 3: More accurate, timely, and local weather forecasts
media:group.media:description:
Predicting the weather is one of the oldest, most complex challenges we face. Traditional numerical weather prediction models are powerful, but they can be slow to run and costly at a global scale. WeatherNext 3 takes a different approach. Built on a fundamentally different architecture, WeatherNext 3 learns directly from real-world observations, including live satellite feeds and ground-level weather station data.
What makes WeatherNext 3 different?
- Hourly refresh: While traditional models typically refresh every six hours, WN3 produces a fresh forecast every single hour. - Hyper-Local resolution: Native 5km resolution for temperature and humidity, enabling better detail for coastal regions, mountains, and urban areas. - Actionable data: Includes variables like 100m wind speeds for wind energy management and detailed cloud/radiation metrics for solar energy planning. - Global reach: Delivering high-resolution insights everywhere.
You can now use WeatherNext 3 through Google Search, Gemini, Google Maps and more.
Learn more: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/introducing-weathernext-3/ Read the full paper: https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/papers/weathernext_3.pdf
Disclaimer: For official weather forecasts, severe weather warnings, and public safety advisories, please refer to your local meteorological agency or national weather service.

media:group.media:title: The mathematics of AI uncertainty
media:group.media:description:
Long before the current wave of large language models, one academic researcher was trying to give machines a sense of their own limitations. Zoubin Ghahramani has spent the last 30 years pioneering a type of intelligence built on the mathematics of uncertainty. Today, as a professor at Cambridge and VP of research at Google DeepMind, Zoubin finds himself at the heart of an interesting debate: will improving machine uncertainty be one of the missing pieces to ever improving AI?
